guarantees.claim: block_addr_limit is driven by a unique case on strength_i: for L128, L224, L256, L384, L512 it is set to the corresponding KeccakRate entry cast to KeccakCountW; for any other value (default) it is set to zero.

assumptions.claim: strength_i must take one of the defined security strength enum values L128, L224, L256, L384, L512 for the block_addr_limit to reflect a valid Keccak rate.
assumptions.risk: If strength_i is any other value, block_addr_limit becomes zero, potentially allowing unbounded or invalid Keccak block addressing that could corrupt data or weaken security guarantees.

uncertain_points.claim: If any KeccakRate entry for L128, L224, L256, L384, L512 is wider than KeccakCountW bits, the cast KeccakCountW'() will silently truncate the value, yielding a wrong block_addr_limit.
uncertain_points.cond: when a KeccakRate parameter width exceeds KeccakCountW
uncertain_points.risk: Truncation could cause incorrect block addressing, leading to secret data exposure or incorrect message authentication code generation.

uncertain_points.claim: The default case assigns block_addr_limit to '0 for any strength_i not matching L128, L224, L256, L384, L512. If other legal strength values exist, or if strength_i becomes corrupt, this fallback may cause the Keccak core to operate with a zero block rate.
uncertain_points.cond: strength_i takes an undefined or illegal value
uncertain_points.risk: A zero block_addr_limit could result in Keccak processing no data or operating in an undefined state, potentially leading to silent data loss or incorrect MAC output.
